README.md:154:A verified eligible `channel.raid` persists a receipt-based 90-second pending handoff with threshold **`min(10, ceil(sqrt(max(1, viewers))))` per side**. Viewers must be a signed finite integer from 0 through 1,000,000. During that window, **`!offer` in source chat** and **`!accept` in target chat** each count distinct authenticated user IDs. One user cannot count on both sides, the configured bot never counts, and blocked participants cannot submit proof. Command text cannot assert a channel or raid membership. Chat location proves participation in that channel, **not actual membership in the incoming Twitch raid**. Claims timestamped before receipt of the pending handoff do not count. This local window is never a Twitch-synchronized countdown.
README.md:156:Both thresholds are required. Concurrent final claims cannot duplicate a stop or transfer. The target becomes holder only at completion; its next hop can then proceed. Target must remain live in the same authoritative stream; both Keepers must retain opt-in and current lifecycle/mark policy eligibility. After a verified handoff opens, its source may close the same authoritative stream: the retained stream ID must match, and the recorded offline boundary must be at/after the persisted signed raid timestamp (which must be at/after that stream start). No newer/different stream qualifies. This also permits closing after a verified manual raid; it does not relax the stricter proof needed to open a handoff when offline arrived before raid confirmation. The target must remain live. Expiry, stream change, opt-out, pause or ban cancels the pending proof permanently when processed, so restoring policy cannot revive old counts. No claim timer, startup network call or public mutation endpoint is added. Expiry is checked on mutations; bounded private participant IDs (at most ten per side) are removed on settlement/cancellation at the next mutation, with no background cleanup promise.

README.md:395:**Hard storage bounds:** each channel document retains at most 16 explicit stream sessions, at most **32 participants per active stream**, at most **five marks per participant / 160 marks per stream**, and at most **160 retained mark records across all sessions**.
